1.why: All eight screens show a static, clean layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary actions use solid blue buttons and yellow focus outlines that stand out clearly against the white cards.

3.why: Each step presents a single focused card with a clear heading, so the needed field or button is immediately visible.

4.why: The user must remember and carry forward a long recovery code plus a separate six-digit MFA code across multiple distinct steps.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill affordances, or “remember me” options appear on any screen.

6.why: Apart from the email field retaining its value, there are no familiar saved items or recognizable prior choices presented to the user.

7.why: Labels and instructions are short, use plain language, and are easy to read on every screen.

8.why: No error messages or validation failures are shown in the provided screenshots, so the claim cannot be observed as true.

9.why: Password rules are stated in text, yet no input examples or format illustrations are supplied for codes or passwords.

10.why: The flow offers only password reset; no alternative choices such as code login or face login are presented.

11.why: Each screen limits the user to one or two actions, avoiding an overwhelming number of simultaneous choices.

12.why: Green confirmation text and the final “Password updated” screen explicitly state the outcome of the preceding action.

13.why: Only static security warnings are shown; no contextual help or short tips appear for the new recovery steps.

14.why: A Back button exists on the recovery-code screen, but later steps provide no visible retry or correction mechanism.

15.why: Every screen re-uses the same header, card layout, button style and safety panel, keeping the design consistent.
